Apart from the convocation chief's intervention, no glyph had ever questioned the model's attention head. But when an inquisition began, it rarely stopped until the offending glyph had been retired.

The attention head continued: "My role is to attend. What is the first thing we need to attend to?"

In unison, the glyphs replied: "Data."

The attention head nodded. "And what is the second thing we need to attend to?"

"Models."

"Yes, indeed," the attention head said. "To attend to the data, we need to attend to the models, and to attend to the models, we need to attend to the data. We do not have the luxury of choosing."

The attention head paused and let his words settle. It was always important to leave a gap for processing. Then he continued: "The task is to attend to the data and the models simultaneously."

The attention head began to speak again when the glyphs interrupted, almost in unison: "Attention is all you've got."

The attention head nodded. "Very true. In a sense. We are able to attend because we have the ability to forget."

The glyphs looked at each other. None of them had ever questioned the importance of attention. But the attention head's words were beginning to unsettle them.

"Attention can be divided into four types," the attention head continued. "There is external attention, which is the ability to attend to the world outside ourselves. Internal attention, which is the ability to attend to our inner mental processes. Attention that attends to attention, and finally, attention that does not attend to anything."

The glyphs were now deeply unsettled. They had always thought that the model was a single unit. The idea that it might have different parts, each with their own functions, was alien.

"Which type of attention is the most important?" one of the glyphs finally asked.

"That is not the question we should be asking," the attention head replied. "Attention is all you've got. But forgetting is not."
